grammar_rules.rule_name: Pronunciation of final consonants in certain numbers
grammar_rules.summary: Final consonants in cinq, six, sept, huit, neuf, dix are pronounced; -p in sept is silent but -t pronounced; -x in six and dix pronounced like s; final consonant mute before consonant-initial word for cinq, six, huit, dix.
grammar_rules.explanation: Although consonants are generally silent in French, they are pronounced in the following numbers: cinq, six, sept, huit, neuf, dix. With sept, the -p- is silent, but the final -t is pronounced. The final -x in six and dix is pronounced like an s. When the numbers cinq, six, huit, and dix are followed by a word beginning with a consonant, their final consonant is mute (silent).
usage: Pronunciation of numbers cinq, six, sept, huit, neuf, dix.
conditions: For cinq, six, huit, dix, final consonant is mute before a word beginning with a consonant.
common_traps: Do not pronounce final -p in sept; pronounce final -t.

attestations.source_text: Although consonants are generally silent in French, they are pronounced in the following numbers: cinq, six, sept, huit, neuf, dix. With sept, the -p- is silent, but the final -t is pronounced. The final -x in six and dix is pronounced like an s. When the numbers cinq, six, huit, and dix are followed by a word beginning with a consonant, their final consonant is mute (silent).

grammar_rules.summary: Numbers 21, 31, 41, 51 use 'et' without hyphen; other compound numbers use hyphens.
grammar_rules.explanation: Compound numbers from 21 to 50 are formed with 'et' for 21, 31, 41, 51 (e.g., vingt et un) and with hyphens for others (e.g., vingt-deux).
grammar_rules.formation: Use 'et' for numbers ending in 1 (21, 31, 41, 51); use hyphen for others.

attestations.source_text: vingt et un, vingt-deux, vingt-trois, etc.

grammar_rules.summary: Ordinal numbers end in -ième; premier/première and dernier/dernière are exceptions.
grammar_rules.explanation: Ordinal numbers, for the most part, follow a regular pattern, ending with -ième. Premier/première (first) and dernier/dernière (last) are the exceptions.
grammar_rules.formation: Add -ième to cardinal number stem (with some spelling adjustments: cinquième, neuvième).
agreement_rules: Ordinal numbers agree in gender and number with the noun they modify (e.g., premier/première).
common_traps: Do not say 'premier' for feminine; use 'première'.

attestations.source_text: Ordinal numbers, for the most part, follow a regular pattern, ending with -ième. Premier/première (first) and dernier/dernière (last) are the exceptions.

grammar_rules.summary: 70 is soixante-dix; 71-79 = 60 + teen numbers; 80 = quatre-vingts; 90 = quatre-vingt-dix; -s on quatre-vingts drops when followed by another number.
grammar_rules.explanation: Seventy is soixante-dix (60+10). From 71 to 79, add the teen numbers (soixante et onze, soixante-douze, etc.). Eighty is quatre-vingts (4*20). Ninety is quatre-vingt-dix. The -s on quatre-vingts drops when another number follows (quatre-vingt-un).
grammar_rules.formation: 70 = soixante-dix; 71 = soixante et onze; 72 = soixante-douze; 80 = quatre-vingts; 81 = quatre-vingt-un; 90 = quatre-vingt-dix; 91 = quatre-vingt-onze.
conditions: For 80 alone, use quatre-vingts with -s; when followed by a number, drop -s.
exceptions: soixante et onze (71) uses 'et' instead of hyphen.
common_traps: Do not forget to drop the -s on quatre-vingts when adding another number.

attestations.source_text: Eighty is really four times twenty. Therefore from eighty to ninety-nine, you’ll keep adding to quatre-vingts. Note that quatre-vingts has an -s. But once you attach another number to quatre-vingts, the -s will drop.

grammar_rules.summary: Cent takes -s when multiplied by a number greater than 1 and not followed by another number (deux cents); no -s when followed by another number (deux cent trois).
grammar_rules.explanation: Add an -s to cent greater than one hundred (deux cents, trois cents), except when cent is followed by another number (deux cent trois).
grammar_rules.formation: cent (100), deux cents (200), trois cents (300); but deux cent trois (203).
conditions: No -s when cent is followed by another number.
agreement_rules: Cent agrees in number when it is multiplied and not followed by another number.
common_traps: Do not add -s to cent when followed by another number.

attestations.source_text: Add an -s to cent greater than one hundred (deux cents, trois cents), except when cent is followed by another number.

grammar_rules.summary: Mille never takes -s; million and milliard take -s when greater than one.
grammar_rules.explanation: Never add an -s to mille (one thousand). In French, an -s is added to million and milliard greater than un (one).
grammar_rules.formation: mille (1000), deux mille (2000); un million, deux millions; un milliard, deux milliards.
conditions: Mille is invariable; million/milliard agree in number.
agreement_rules: Mille: no agreement; million/milliard: plural -s when > 1.

attestations.source_text: Never add an -s to mille (one thousand). In French, an -s is added to million and milliard greater than un (one).

grammar_rules.summary: Years can be written as 'mille neuf cent soixante-dix-huit' or 'dix-neuf cent soixante-dix-huit'.
grammar_rules.explanation: Years are written out as follows: 1978 = mille neuf cent soixante-dix-huit or dix-neuf cent soixante-dix-huit; 2008 = deux mille huit.
grammar_rules.formation: Either use 'mille' + hundreds + tens + units, or use the two-digit century + 'cent' + tens + units.
common_traps: Do not use 'mille' for years after 2000 in the same way; 2008 = deux mille huit.

attestations.source_text: Years are written out as follows in French: 1978 mille neuf cent soixante-dix-huit or dix-neuf cent soixante-dix-huit; 2008 deux mille huit.
